name: mp-02-stairs-crowd
why: Likeness plus Oktoberfest visitors sharing the staircase - crowd in the same space as the subject, not only far below.
prompt: Photorealistic candid street photograph. A powerfully built German man in his mid-forties walks down the broad stone staircase below the colossal bronze Bavaria statue at the Theresienwiese in Munich, during Oktoberfest. His appearance: a strongly receding hairline, ash-blonde hair going grey, combed tight and straight back and gathered into a small low bun at the nape; a neat pointed goatee and moustache, blonde shading to grey, reaching a couple of centimetres below the chin; rimless eyeglasses with slim orange temple arms; a small stud earring. Heavy muscular build, very broad shoulders, thick neck, barrel chest, a slight softness at the waist, about 1.85 m tall. He wears a plain black long-sleeved button shirt with the sleeves turned back over thick forearms, slim black jeans and black leather boots. He is mid-stride, one hand loosely on the stone balustrade, glancing out over the fairground with a faint half-smile. Around him on the same wide steps, dozens of Oktoberfest visitors climb and descend: women in dirndls with patterned aprons, men in lederhosen with checked shirts and felt hats, families, friends in groups of three and four, some carrying jackets, some photographing the view. They pass him on both sides at different distances, giving a busy but unhurried flow of people across the whole staircase. Behind and above, the green-black bronze of the Bavaria and the sandstone columns of the Ruhmeshalle. Below and beyond, the Wiesn: rows of enormous beer tents with painted facades, flag poles, a Ferris wheel and rides, dense crowds in the avenues. Bright overcast daylight, soft even light, faint haze. Shot on 35mm, natural colour, the man sharp in the foreground, the crowd falling gently out of focus with distance.
